section_summary: This concluding section contains Japanese legal texts governing opium, narcotics, coca, Indian hemp, addiction treatment, licensing, recordkeeping, import and export, and penalties in colonial Taiwan. It also includes 1937–1938 correspondence transmitting and explaining these regulations to the U.S. Treasury Department. The final documents report narcotics smuggling in 1938 and identify seven alleged smugglers, their routes, offenses, and case dispositions.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Opium Regulations, Articles 18–47 and supplementary provisions (continued)
subfiles.to: Opium licensees, medical and pharmaceutical professionals, and the public in Taiwan
subfiles.about: Regulations governing opium-paste retailing, medicinal opium, smoking implements, licensing, addiction examinations, fees, and penalties.
subfiles.summary: The continued regulations restrict retail opium-paste sales to licensed smokers or their certified agents and require detailed purchase books and dealer accounts. They regulate medicinal opium transactions, export permits, scientific use, storage, disposal, professional reporting, and the manufacture and sale of smoking implements. Later provisions address lost or amended licenses, compulsory examinations or hospitalization of suspected addicts, administrative fees, business-license cancellation, criminal penalties, and transitional arrangements effective January 9, 1929.

subfiles.title: Regulations of the Taiwan Government General Opium Addiction Correction Institute
subfiles.to: Opium Addiction Correction Institute and Police Affairs Bureau personnel
subfiles.about: Establishes the Opium Addiction Correction Institute and defines its organization and duties.
subfiles.summary: Instruction 3 places the Opium Addiction Correction Institute under the Police Affairs Bureau to correct addiction under the Taiwan Opium Ordinance, with director, medical officers, dispensers and clerks; effective January 15, 1930.

subfiles.title: Opium Addiction Correction Procedures
subfiles.to: Provincial governors, bureau chiefs, rehabilitation institutes, and hospital directors
subfiles.about: Prescribes procedures, capacity limits, charges, notifications, and forms for institutional treatment of opium addicts.
subfiles.summary: Instruction 46: governors hospitalize younger and less severely addicted persons first, with communication duties, capacity limits and monthly reports of admissions, discharges, results and fees; the standard charge is sixty sen daily; admission, discharge and fee forms attached.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Narcotics Control Regulations, Ordinance No. 71
subfiles.to: Narcotics manufacturers, importers, exporters, medical and pharmaceutical professionals, cultivators, and the public
subfiles.about: Comprehensive regulations controlling narcotic manufacture, movement, possession, coca cultivation, Indian hemp, inspections, treatment, and penalties.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines controlled narcotics and generally limits them to medical and scientific use. It establishes permits, labeling, accounts, and reports for manufacture, import, export, movement through Taiwan, sale, possession, and storage. Separate provisions govern coca cultivation and apply related controls to Indian hemp, while further articles cover losses, addiction reporting and treatment, inspections, administrative prohibitions, and criminal penalties. The ordinance took effect on December 25, 1929 and repealed the earlier Taiwan morphine and cocaine regulations.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning Ordinances Nos. 3 and 5 and amendments to the Taiwan Opium Regulations
subfiles.from: Jiro Morioka, Director General of Administration, Government General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Replies to a request for copies of two opium ordinances and supplies the substance of the 1936 amendments.
subfiles.summary: Morioka refers Warner to the "Opium System of Taiwan" pamphlet for Ordinance 3 of 1928 and explains Ordinance 5 of December 5, 1936 amended Articles 13 and 15 to punish coercing, inducing or assisting unlicensed opium use or possession, effective April 22, 1937.

subfiles.title: Department of State transmittal of the “Opium System of Taiwan” pamphlet
subfiles.about: Transmits a consular despatch and Japanese-language regulations relevant to the Marihuana Tax Act of 1937.
subfiles.summary: State sends Treasury duplicates of a December 3, 1937 Taihoku despatch and the 1936 "Opium System of Taiwan," marking Ordinance 71 provisions on cannabis, narcotics transport, coca and Indian hemp, and relaying that Indian hemp isn't imported for lack of demand.

subfiles.title: Translation of Marked Portions of “Opium System of Taiwan”
subfiles.about: Summarizes the marked narcotics-control provisions in the Japanese-language Taiwan pamphlet.
subfiles.summary: The translation outlines requirements for narcotics import and export permits, certified export documentation, permit expiration, shipment-completion notices, bonded storage, and recordkeeping. It also summarizes permits and records for coca cultivation and annual reporting by coca growers. The final provision applies equivalent controls to the cultivation of Indian hemp.

subfiles.title: Department of State transmittal concerning Ordinance No. 5 of 1936
subfiles.about: Transmits a consular despatch and the Taiwan Government General’s explanation of the 1936 amendment to the opium ordinance.
subfiles.summary: Under the Narcotic Drugs Import and Export Act, State forwards the December 16, 1937 Taihoku despatch and Morioka's December 13 letter on Ordinance 5, noting the Opium Ordinance went to Treasury in 1930 and no full English translation exists.
keywords: Narcotic Drugs Import and Export Act

subfiles.title: Narcotic Smuggling and Smugglers in Taiwan in 1938
subfiles.about: Reports information supplied by Taiwan authorities concerning illicit narcotics traffic and suspected smugglers during 1938.
subfiles.summary: Warner says the Government General supplied information and a list of narcotics offenders for visa checks and lookout notices; smuggling wasn't widespread and opium imports from China nearly ceased after the conflict and halt of junk traffic.

subfiles.title: List of Narcotic Smugglers Uncovered in 1938 in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Taihoku Police authorities through the Department of Foreign Affairs, Taiwan Government General
subfiles.about: Lists seven alleged narcotics smugglers and records their identities, routes, criminal histories, quantities involved, and case dispositions.
subfiles.summary: List of 1938 narcotics smugglers, all Formosan Chinese, including To Gin-bun and Chin Shin-i, on routes from Amoy via Keelung or Dairen via Kobe, carrying crude or smoking opium; most cases went to the Taihoku Chief Procurator in December 1938, while Chin remained under investigation.

subfiles.title: Department of State transmittal of Despatch No. 60 on illicit narcotics traffic
subfiles.about: Forwards the Taihoku consular report and enclosure on illicit narcotics traffic in Taiwan during 1938.
subfiles.summary: State sends Treasury duplicates of Despatch 60 (March 17, 1939) on illicit narcotics traffic and identified smuggling cases in Taiwan in 1938.
